note: Rewritten from the original description of Termes angustipennis by Sjöstedt (1900), which includes a Latin diagnosis and a German description; only the alate was described, soldiers and workers were not recorded; wing-width figures omitted because of incomplete OCR; specimen records not translated.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Only the alate is known. The alate closely resembles T. buchholzi, from which it differs in the longer and narrower wings; the difference lies mainly in the length/width ratio of the wing rather than in the branching pattern of the veins. The point at which the media meets the submedia lies near the base of the wing rather than at its middle, so that usually only 2–3 accessory branches occur between this point and the wing base; the proximally situated junction and the small number of accessory branches are the most conspicuous and most easily observed venational characters of the species. The course of the veins is broadly the same in the two species, the differences being concentrated in the length/width ratio of the wing and in the density of the accessory branches; the wing shape of this species therefore appears narrow and elongate. Wingspan 55–57 mm, body length with wings 29–31 mm, wing length 26–27 mm, body length with head 12–14 mm.
